The two failed attaches (C127, C050) both gave NO_CONNECTION. Looking at the candidate catalog, C127 shows the plate floating above the baseplate (no stud contact) and C050 also shows it offset/floating. The previews that show the plate actually resting ON the studs with proper alignment are the ones where the plate is centered on the grid. C056 shows plate at front edge resting on studs. C101 shows plate resting on studs near center-back. C128 shows plate resting on studs left side. C181 shows plate resting centered on studs.

The target top view: blue chassis runs vertically centered, overhanging the front (bottom in top view). The plate is 2x6 oriented along the long axis of the 6x8 baseplate. In top view the baseplate is 6 wide x 8 tall. The blue plate occupies columns 3-4 (center 2 columns) and rows 2-8 roughly, overhanging front.

I need a candidate where the plate sits centered on the long axis and overhangs the front. Looking at previews: C056 is at the front edge horizontal-ish? Hard. C101 shows plate near center oriented along long axis resting on studs. C181 shows plate centered resting on studs but maybe not overhanging front.

Rather than guess blindly, the NO_CONNECTION means no stud alignment. The previews that look "grounded on studs" (plate sitting flush within stud grid) are C056, C101, C128, C181. C127 and C050 looked floating/offset.

The target requires overhang at front. C101 shows plate sitting on studs at back-center with front studs visible — but target overhangs front. Actually overhang isn't strictly required for connection; the chassis just needs to be a 2x6 blue plate centered longitudinally. The wheels attach to sides.

Let me try C101 which appears to show the plate resting properly on studs centered along the long axis. If that connects, good. I'll commit to C101.
